newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing says fiscal discipline key for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing says fiscal discipline key for EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing on Monday stressed once again the German central bank's belief in the importance of strict fiscal discipline to the single currency project.

In the text of a speech to be delivered at a conference here, Issing said European citizens, especially Germans, would be paying closer attention to the preparations for monetary union as the planned launch date of January 1999 approached.
"Solid state finances are in themselves an expression of, and precondition for, political stability. At the same time they are also an essential counterpart to monetary stability," Issing said.
"For this reason budgetary convergence criteria rightly represent a hurdle for entry to the currency union."
Issing said budgetary stability most be secured both during the preparations for curreny union and after its launch.

"It is precisely for this reason that the finance minister (Theo Waigel) is insisting on a stability pact which threatens harsh sanctions in the cases of lapses in budgetary policy ...," Issing added.

Issing concluded by citing Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer's recent words on the single currency project: "Political goals can only be achieved in harmony with the economy, not in opposition to it. Deeds alone, rather than words will decide."
